category: 2026 DRC-Uganda-France BDBV Outbreak (Active — PHEIC; deadliest and largest ever recorded in DRC)
killed: 2,325 confirmed DRC / 2 confirmed Uganda = 2,327 confirmed total
injured: 2,620 surviving confirmed cases; 730 currently hospitalized in isolation (DRC); 1,040 recovered; Uganda outbreak closed 28 July with 18 recoveries
source: DRC Ministry of Health / ECDC / CIDRAP / UN News — 16–17 August 2026
note: DRC: 4,945 confirmed cases across 55 of 151 health zones in 6 provinces (Ituri ~85% of cases, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uélé, Tshopo, and Bas-Uélé) as of 15 August, published 16 August; 2,325 confirmed deaths; crude CFR ~47%, up from ~20% in early June. Uganda: 20 confirmed cases (2 deaths, 18 recoveries), outbreak formally declared over 28 July 2026. France: 1 case, recovered and discharged 4 July, no secondary transmission. WHO estimates true DRC case count could be up to 4x higher than reported. 60-70% of deaths occur in communities away from treatment centers. 155 confirmed cases among healthcare workers with 45 deaths (29% CFR). It took 67 days to cross 1,000 deaths (22 July) and under a month to reach 2,000 (early August) — the fastest fatal surge in Ebola's recorded history, versus 142 days for the 2014-16 West Africa epidemic to reach 1,000 deaths. On 16 August the death toll surpassed the 2,299 deaths of DRC's 2018-2020 Kivu outbreak, making this the deadliest Ebola outbreak in the country's history and the second-largest ever recorded worldwide behind the 2014-16 West Africa epidemic. UN humanitarian chief Tom Fletcher said on 14 August the outbreak was killing one person every 30 minutes and released an additional $30.5M from CERF. WHO TAG-CVP recommended Ervebo (rVSV-ZEBOV) for a Phase 3 trial against Bundibugyo (7 August), with WHO-DRC trial talks advancing but not yet launched as of 17 August. US pledged an additional $242M (5 August), bringing total US assistance above $512M. A second WHO IHR Emergency Committee meeting was scheduled for 18 August.
